article_sentences: A Sub-Inspector and Station House Officer (SHO) of Maker.
Police Station in Saran district has been suspended for pointing a gun at the flood victims during the distribution of relief materials.
The video of a SHO pointing a gun and showing footwear to the flood victims went viral on social media.
The incident happened on Sunday (October 4, 2026) afternoon near Reva Ghat.
Late at night, around 11 p.m., Saran Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Roshan Kumar issued the suspension order.

“A video is circulating on various social media platforms showing Sub-Inspector Sangram Kumar Singh, Station House Officer (SHO) of Maker, pointing his pistol at the public during the distribution of flood relief materials; prima facie, this conduct reflects gross negligence in the discharge of his duties, indiscipline, and arbitrary behaviour,” SSP Roshan said in the press statement.
He added, “For the negligence displayed, Sub-Inspector Sangram Kumar Singh, SHO of Maker Police Station, is hereby suspended with immediate effect and placed on subsistence allowance.
During suspension, he will be designated at headquarters.
Subsistence allowance will be payable subject to his attendance.”
In the video, the SI is seen standing on top of a pickup truck loaded with rations and arguing with flood-affected villagers lined up for relief material.
Some villagers just stepped out of line to grab rations when the SI first flashed his footwear and then pulled out his gun, aiming it at the flood victims.

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) attacked the State government over the incident by posting a message on the social media account X along with the video of the SI, asserting that those in power are treating common people like insects.

article_sentences: The river Gandak has begun receding in Bihar as the state government suspended seven engineers over flood response lapses.
The action underscores mounting scrutiny of embankment management while relief work continues across six affected districts.

The water level of river Gandak in Bihar has started receding quickly, even as the state government on Sunday suspended seven engineers and began departmental proceedings against another official for alleged negligence in handling the recent floods, according to an official statement.
The Water Resources Department said there was currently no pressure on embankments, while seepage and piping problems had been resolved.
It also said materials had been stocked at breach sites to protect vulnerable stretches.
At Rewaghat in Saran, the Gandak's water level has fallen by 177 cm from its record high and is now 50 cm below the danger mark, the department said in a statement issued on Sunday evening.
At Lalganj in Vaishali, the level has dropped by 130 cm but remains 52 cm above the danger mark.
It is expected to fall below the danger mark within the next 24 hours, the release added.

The Gandak had recorded unprecedented water levels after heavy rainfall in adjoining Nepal and Uttar Pradesh, with record highs reported at Devghat in Nepal and at Bagaha, Dumariaghat, Rewaghat and Lalganj in Bihar.

The department said inspections had found laxity and delays in the emergency response by some engineers, including inadequate mobilisation of manpower and materials and poor coordination with locals and elected representatives.
"Seven engineers, including two executive engineers, have been suspended with immediate effect.
Departmental proceedings have also been ordered against Muzaffarpur chief engineer Kumar Manoj Gupta over alleged negligence following damage to the Champaran embankment," the statement said.

So there is no illegality; there is nothing to object to; there should be no objection in this regard.”

stories.title: Odisha government announces to hold student union election after a gap of eight years

article_sentences: The Odisha government on Monday (Octobeer 5, 2026) announced that student union elections will be held on higher education campuses after a gap of eight years.
The elections will be completed within the next 10 days.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi approved conducting student union elections, which involves massive security arrangement in view of possible violence on campuses.

Speaking after his meeting with the Odisha Chief Minister, State Higher Education Minister Suryabanshi Suraj said, “the detailed timeline and complete information will be provided by the department very soon.
A final decision has been taken to hold the elections before the Dussehra holidays, and colleges will issue their own notifications on the October 7, 2026.
Nominations will be filed on the October 9, and the elections will be held on the October 15 and the oath-taking ceremony will be held on the morning of October 16.”
“We believe that conducting these elections is important because today’s students and student leaders are the future leaders of Odisha.

This process will help them understand democratic responsibilities, the importance of democracy, and constitutional values, preparing them to take up leadership roles in the future,” said Mr. Suryabanshi.
Stating that the this is a significant step, the Minister informed “student union elections had been suspended since 2017.
We had also promised in our election manifesto that these elections would be conducted.
After formation of our government in 2024, we spent 2025 addressing various issues on campuses, and in 2026 we are now moving ahead with student union elections.”
He said to ensure peaceful and orderly elections, the Supreme Court’s 2005 verdict and the recommendations of the J. M Lyngdoh Committee, which were followed earlier, will continue to be implemented.

stories.title: Trump wrongly cites Indian election to call US voting process ‘corrupt’
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 5 : In an apparent faux pas, US President Donald Trump mentioned India in a social media post to claim that the electoral process in the US was "corrupt", when there were no elections in India, and the post clearly appeared to be about the presidential election in Brazil. In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump claimed that "125 million people voted in India's Presidential elections and the results came out shortly after the vote closed". "Voting in America is CORRUPT," Trump said, referring to the weeks taken for the counting of votes in elections in US cities and states. "125 Million People voted today in the first round of India's Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY," Trump said. "In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is CORRUPT," the US president said. The reference to India appeared to be a possible mix-up with Brazil. Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with 125.27 million valid votes recorded, according to the country's electoral authority. Results began to be released at 5 pm, when voting ended, and were updated as ballots were received and processed. Brazilians voted in the presidential election pitting incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. With neither of them able to secure a majority in the first round, the run-off election will be held on October 25. India, meanwhile, did not hold a presidential election. President Droupadi Murmu, who took office in July 2022, is the current President of India. Also, Indians do not directly elect their President. The President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states and union territories through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. In India's regular elections, voters directly elect members of the Lok Sabha (lower house of the Parliament) and state legislative assemblies. The Prime Minister is then appointed by the President, usually the leader of the party or coalition commanding a majority in the Lok Sabha, while chief ministers are appointed by state governors, usually the leader of the party or coalition commanding a majority in the state assembly. India had nearly 980 million registered electors in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Trump has previously cited Indian elections, particularly the country's voter identification system, to push for electoral reforms in the US. In August, Trump said India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had spoken with officials from his administration and asked how US elections can be held without a valid photo identification card. The US president made these remarks to drum up support for the SAVE America Act, which would require Americans to show proof of citizenship to register to vote, impose a nationwide voter identification requirement and severely limit voting by mail. "Earlier this month, India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration â€" How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID," Trump said on August 17. "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than one per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document." "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now," he had then asserted in a social media post. PTI

body: Jerusalem, Oct 5: The Omani co-pilot who attempted to crash a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv had planned to deliberately crash the aircraft into a building or another plane at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, according to reports in the Israeli media.

Hamam Al-Hammami, an Omani first officer who is currently under arrest, reportedly told investigators in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) that he intended to continue operating flydubai Flight 1073 normally after killing the aircraft's captain, Indian pilot Smit Machchhar.

According to the reports, his plan was to obtain the necessary landing clearances without arousing suspicion and then crash the aircraft into a building or another jet at the airport in an attack resembling the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Quoting sources, Ynet reported that Al-Hammami told investigators that he intended to initiate the plan while the aircraft was over Jordan and approaching Israel.
By waiting until the final stage of the flight, he believed that he would prevent anyone from understanding what was happening in time to alert authorities or stop him from carrying out the plan.

The reports further said that Al-Hammami had also told investigators that if he was unable to crash the aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport, he planned to target a skyscraper in Tel Aviv or one of the US military bases in Jordan.
However, the plan was thwarted after Captain Machchhar, despite suffering serious injuries, fought back against the co-pilot.
The Indian pilot managed to send distress signals and open the cockpit door, enabling crew members and passengers to intervene and restrain Al-Hammami.
Two off-duty pilots travelling on the aircraft subsequently helped regain control of the plane and safely landed it in Saudi Arabia, preventing the attack from being carried out.
Captain Machchhar, who is currently receiving treatment at a hospital in Abu Dhabi, recounted the attack during a conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday.
He said that Al-Hammami had asked to pray shortly before attacking him with a crash axe.
Machchhar recalled that the first blow landed heavily on his head and that he initially believed the aircraft itself had suffered some kind of impact.
At first, Captain Machchhar said he thought the plane had been hit.
However, as the assault continued, he realised that the danger was coming from the person sitting beside him in the cockpit.
"The blows kept coming.
I realised that it's not the aircraft; it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said.

Sources cited by Israel's Channel 12 reportedly said that Al-Hammami had initially intended to carry out the plan in July but postponed the operation at the last moment because he was friends with one of the crew members.
Reports also stated that Al-Hammami had flown to Ben Gurion Airport several times in the months before the incident after joining flydubai.
According to the reports, he told investigators that during a visit to Israel in June, he concentrated on gathering information and preparing for the alleged attack.
A Channel 13 report said that the Omani co-pilot had planned the attack even before joining flydubai, the low-cost Emirati airline that operates flights between Israel and the UAE.
"I looked into which airline flies to Tel Aviv.
That's why I chose flydubai.
I planned it even before I was accepted," he reportedly told investigators.
The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera reported that after attacking Captain Machchhar, Al-Hammami switched off the aircraft's engines and pushed the rudders forward.
According to the report, the actions caused the aircraft to lose around 16,000 feet of altitude in less than a minute, bringing it close to the speed of sound.

As the investigation into the flydubai incident continues, preliminary details have also raised questions about possible security lapses and the process through which the co-pilot was cleared to operate the flight.
Officials have already said that Al-Hammami's own country had previously barred him from flying because of concerns related to his alleged extremist views.

Questions have also been raised over how an Omani citizen, from an Arab country that does not have diplomatic relations with Israel, was permitted to operate a flight carrying Israeli passengers to Tel Aviv.
Al-Hammami, 29, is an Omani citizen whose father is Omani and mother Syrian.
He had lived in Syria during the country's civil war and had reportedly posted messages online expressing support for al-Qaeda.
It also remains unclear how flydubai failed to identify Al-Hammami as a potential security concern before allowing him to serve as a co-pilot on flights to Israel.
Regional officials told the Associated Press that Emirati authorities had shared information concerning passengers and crew members, including their nationalities.
The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to publicly discuss details of the ongoing investigation.
Israel's domestic security agency, Shin Bet, said that the Transportation Ministry is responsible for vetting passenger lists received from foreign flights.

Transportation Minister Miri Regev, in a post on X, said that responsibility for flight security lies with the security agencies and that her ministry had not been provided with a passenger list or received any warnings concerning the flight.
Sharing passenger and crew information is considered a standard aviation procedure.

However, Dvir Rubenstien, head of aviation security at Israel's Transportation Ministry, told Army Radio that the ministry relies on security checks carried out locally and does not possess the tools or capacity to independently conduct checks on every passenger travelling on every flight.
--IANS.

stories.summary: Patna, Oct 5 : As JD(U) candidate Neeraj Kumar is set to file his nomination for the Bihar Legislative Council elections on Monday, the party expressed confidence that the NDA will win all eight seats in the upcoming biennial polls, describing the contest as a one-sided affair. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced October 23 as the date for the biennial elections to eight seats of the Bihar Legislative Council. JD(U) Bihar president Umesh Kushwaha said the NDA would secure victory on all eight seats. “The NDA will win all eight seats, and it will be a one-sided victory. No one is in contention. You know how the NDA performed in the 2025 Assembly elections. This is based on the trust of our workers, and we have placed our trust in them,” Kushwaha said. JD(U) spokesperson Rajiv Ranjan also expressed confidence in Neeraj Kumar, saying he would continue the party's winning streak. “He will continue the winning streak. The way he has consistently served the party and the people, he has also been vocal in the Legislative Council. He has been recognised as a popular leader since the party's inception, and this will undoubtedly benefit him in the Legislative Council election," he said. The election for eight seats in the Teacher and Graduate constituencies of the Legislative Council has generated considerable interest even before the nomination process. Differences have emerged within both the NDA and the Grand Alliance camps. Within the NDA, differences have surfaced in the JD(U) over the Patna Graduate constituency. At the same time, the Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM), a key constituent of the NDA, has reportedly expressed resentment over not being allotted a seat. The contest has also gained significance amid the ongoing war of words between JD(U) MLA from Mokama, Anant Singh, and Neeraj Kumar. Neeraj recently met JD(U) national president Nitish Kumar on Saturday and sought his blessings. The meeting is being viewed as significant ahead of the MLC election. Following the meeting, Neeraj said he would file his nomination on October 5. The internal standoff between Anant Singh and Neeraj Kumar has intensified in recent days. Anant Singh on Sunday claimed that he would ensure Neeraj's defeat in the election at all costs, even if it resulted in his expulsion from the party. Meanwhile, Bihar Health Minister and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son, Nishant Kumar, urged young party workers to unite and actively campaign for Neeraj Kumar to ensure his victory. Interacting with party workers, Nishant said, “Neeraj Kumar is a dedicated and experienced party colleague with an unwavering commitment to socialist ideology. He has consistently raised public grievances and issues concerning the welfare of his constituency.” On the other hand, Anant Singh maintained that the dispute between him and Neeraj Kumar was a personal matter and not a party issue. He also cautioned that leaders considering intervening in the dispute could be making a mistake. --IANS

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 5 : The Supreme Court will hear petitions on Monday challenging whether Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar can single-handedly exercise powers constitutionally designated for the entire multi-member poll panel. As per the cause list published on the official website of the apex court, a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is slated to take up the matter. The matter was mentioned before the CJI earlier on September 29 by senior advocate Vikas Singh, following which the CJI said: "List it next week." The plea seeks enforcement of the collective decision-making framework governing the ECI and a writ in the nature of quo warranto concerning the authority under which the CEC has reportedly acted in the name of the poll panel. The petition contends that Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the “Commission” and not in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It further relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which provides for collective decision-making, with matters on which there is no unanimity to be decided by majority. The plea has relied upon contemporaneous written communications and file notings attributed to Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who allegedly recorded at least 14 objections between October 2025 and August 2026 concerning decisions and steps allegedly taken in the name of the ECI without their approval. The objections, as detailed in the petition, relate to communications and orders allegedly issued without the poll body's approval, the absence of agendas before and minutes after meetings, foreign travel undertaken without approval, changes to Form 6, access to the electoral roll database and filing of appeals before tribunals in West Bengal. The plea also refers to concerns reportedly raised by the two Election Commissioners over the "gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database", and changes in the work allocation of the poll body's IT establishment. The petitioner has sought a declaration that powers vested in the ECI under Article 324 cannot be exercised or represented as an act of the poll body except in accordance with the constitutional and statutory framework governing the Commission. The plea also seeks declaratory and mandatory directions to ensure compliance with the collective decision-making framework, besides production and preservation of relevant records concerning the disputed decisions. Meanwhile, the ECI has maintained that the reported differences between the Commissioners do not amount to an institutional "rupture" and that internal objections and written notes are established mechanisms in a multi-member constitutional body. --IANS

article_sentences: The Supreme Court allowed 11 Delhi Gymkhana Club members to move the Delhi High Court against the Centre's takeover and eviction action.
The order reopens their challenge while leaving maintainability and other legal objections to be decided there.

The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Delhi High Court to consider a plea by 11 members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club against the Centre's decision to take over the club's 27.3-acre premises and the subsequent eviction proceedings.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told that the Delhi High Court had earlier declined to entertain the plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre's decision.
The court then allowed the members to move the High Court, subject to objections that may be raised by the other side on maintainability and other legal grounds.
Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the club members, told the Supreme Court that the High Court had asked them to obtain a clarification from the apex court that they could also approach it.
Singh had earlier submitted that the club was currently being run by a committee nominated by the central government and therefore could not fight a legal battle against the government.

In a separate case on September 3, the Centre told the Delhi High Court that it would not take any coercive action till September 16 in connection with the club's eviction from its Safdarjung Road premises.

The High Court was hearing petitions by club member Vijay Khurana and others seeking a stay on the June 29 show-cause notice issued to the club's management by an estate officer of the Land and Development Office.

In their petition filed through lawyer Nitin Saluja, Vipin Aggarwal and 10 other members sought the quashing of the resumption notification issued by the Land and Development Office on May 22 and the show-cause notice issued by the estate officer on June 29.
The Supreme Court's order now allows the members to pursue their plea before the Delhi High Court, where questions on maintainability and other objections can also be considered.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to fast-track a nearly four-decade-old compensation dispute arising from the 1988 Ahmedabad air crash that killed 133 people, after Air India sought an urgent hearing in a case that could potentially reshape how compensation is calculated in air-crash claims.
A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to list the matter before Justices Aravind Kumar and N.V. Anjaria, who had earlier heard the long-running dispute.
“List before the bench presided by Justice Aravind Kumar,” the CJI said.
Mint reported earlier on Monday that Air India had sought an early hearing of the case, which was last heard in December 2025 but was not taken up thereafter.
The airline subsequently moved an application seeking an early hearing.

At the heart of the dispute is a question that has remained unresolved for decades: should compensation for victims of an air crash be calculated using principles developed by the Supreme Court for road accidents under the Motor Vehicles Act, or should aviation accidents be governed by a separate framework?
Written submissions filed by victims’ families and reviewed by Mint argue that Motor Vehicles Act principles should not automatically apply to air crashes.
The claimants contend that passengers have little or no control over the operation, maintenance or safety of an aircraft and generally have no knowledge of its technical functioning.
They argue that compensation should instead be determined under ordinary principles of tort law, with victims receiving full or just compensation.

The submissions also seek consideration of factors such as actual income, future earning capacity and changes in earnings over time, rather than relying solely on standardised formulas developed for road accidents.

The Supreme Court’s decision to hear the matter comes against the backdrop of last year’s Air India crash that killed 260 people, with several pleas concerning air safety and the crash investigation pending before the court.
An email seeking Air India’s response on today’s court proceedings remained unanswered at press time.

article_sentences: Noting a systemic policing failure, the court stressed that law enforcement must create a strong deterrent so that women feel secure traveling alone at night.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday stressed the imperative to instil fear in the minds of goons committing crimes against women, remarking that a perception persists that women remain unsafe in the capital, particularly within specific vulnerable pockets.
The top court voiced the observation whilst presiding over a suo motu matter initiated following recent sexual assault cases across the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR).
"We have to work together.
We must ensure that every woman in Delhi-NCR should feel safe even at 11 pm, whether travelling on the roads or the metro," a bench comprising Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran noted.

"What is important is to prevent a crime, not what you do after a crime is committed," the bench stated, underscoring that law enforcement agencies must cultivate a strong deterrent amongst anti-social elements prone to committing such offences.
The bench, which was conducting proceedings under the suo motu title 'In Re: Recent rape incidents in Delhi NCR', remarked that "rape is something which is not at all acceptable to any society".

The apex court had previously taken suo motu cognisance on September 28 after reviewing media reports concerning atrocities against minor girls and women across Delhi-NCR, observing that the series of incidents pointed to a systemic failure on the part of policing authorities.

The court took note of multiple incidents, including the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in Delhi, the gang-rape and murder of a teenage girl in the Swaroop Nagar locality of the capital, and the sexual assault of a minor inside a moving sleeper bus that law enforcement failed to stop despite the vehicle covering a distance exceeding 47 km from Greater Noida to Delhi.
